unit_pptx_name: Term 4 Week 6 - Learning from Powerful Speakers - Year 5-6 Literacy.pptx
anchor: Claim it. Prove it. Sell it. Say it. The writing anchor plus a microphone (say it), and the speech rule: write for the ear. Final piece: a rehearsed persuasive speech delivered to a live audience.

lessons.title: Read It or Hear It?
lessons.focus: Compare a persuasive text read silently with the same ideas spoken; start the Persuasive Speaker's Toolkit. Critical feature: write for the ear: short sentences, repeated key words, you and we.

lessons.title: Severn's Six Minutes
lessons.focus: Severn Cullis-Suzuki at the 1992 Earth Summit: message, audience and what she wants us to think, feel and do. Critical feature: a speaker earns the right to be heard by saying who they are and why it matters to them.

lessons.title: Malala's Voice
lessons.focus: Malala Yousafzai at the UN in 2013: personal story and lists of three. Critical feature: a true story makes a big idea feel real.

lessons.title: Greta's Fire
lessons.focus: Greta Thunberg at the UN in 2019: short sentences, direct address and tone. Critical feature: a short sentence after a long one lands like a punch.

lessons.title: The Dream Speech
lessons.focus: Martin Luther King Jr. in 1963: repetition and imagery building a vision. Critical feature: repeated openings build rhythm and make the audience feel the dream.
